description:
Blueprint Loader lets you install blueprint mods for Minecraft Dungeons II!

Drop mods into your ~mods folder and they are loaded automatically every time a level loads, without replacing any game files. A template project for making your own mods is available separately.

Mod Menu

Blueprint Loader adds a Mods tab to the game's settings, with a list of every mod you have installed. Open it from the settings, with the MODS button on the main menu, with the Mods button in the System tab of the in-game menu, or with a key of your choice.

Select a mod to see its details, with a switch to turn it on or off. Mods with settings have a settings button that opens their page, and your changes are saved automatically. "Reset mod" puts that mod's settings back to their defaults.

Mods that are on Nexus Mods show when an update is out, with a green arrow next to their name and on the MODS button. Click "Update available" to open the mod's page.

If a mod crashes the game, Blueprint Loader turns it off and tells you the next time you start the game. You can turn it back on in the Mods tab.

Blueprint Loader has these settings of its own:

  • Main Menu Label: shows the Blueprint Loader name and version in the top left of the main menu
  • Main Menu Mods Button: shows the MODS button on the main menu
  • System Menu Mods Button: shows a Mods button in the System tab of the in-game menu
  • Open Mods Key: opens the Mods tab from anywhere
  • Open To: opens a mod's page straight away when using the key

Install

There are two files on this page. To play with mods, you only need Blueprint Loader. Blueprint Mod Template is only for making mods.

  1. Download the Blueprint Loader file.
  2. Close the game, and fully close the Minecraft Launcher if you use it.
  3. Open your Minecraft Dungeons II Paks folder.
    • Steam: Right click the game in your library, then Manage > Browse local files, then open Dungeons\Content\Paks
    • Minecraft Launcher: C:\XboxGames\Minecraft Dungeons II\Content\Dungeons\Content\Paks
    If you picked a different install folder in the Minecraft Launcher, it is Minecraft Dungeons II\Content\Dungeons\Content\Paks inside that folder.
  4. Create a folder called ~mods inside the Paks folder if there is not one already.
  5. Open the zip and move the BlueprintLoader folder inside it into ~mods, so the files end up like this: Paks\~mods\BlueprintLoader\BlueprintLoader_P.pak

Uninstall

Delete the BlueprintLoader folder from ~mods.

Making mods

Download the Blueprint Mod Template file to make your own blueprint mods. It includes an example mod with settings, a build script that cooks and packs your mod into the files needed, and a readme covering mod info, settings pages, settings that show or hide based on other settings, side columns, translations, update checks, load priority, turning mods off, popups, the rules and limitations.

Support

If you need help, join my Discord!
